assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision CMB mapping with WMAP turned cosmology into a quantitative science: it fixed the age, geometry and matter-energy budget of the universe (including dark energy and dark matter fractions) and tested the primordial perturbation spectrum. This is a clues-from-nature discovery with direct existential meaning, and it is the observational backbone for the dark energy question I care about.
assessment.attribution: The mission PI (Bennett), the leading theorist/analyst of cosmological parameters (Spergel) and the instrument/experimental-design lead (Page) form a workable three-person configuration. Other WMAP and COBE-lineage team leaders (e.g. Wilkinson, deceased) and Planck leaders complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based experiments, with a stable interpretation (LambdaCDM). Recognition is not premature, and the passage of time since COBE (2006) and Peebles (2019) is a mild issue of redundancy rather than doubt.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and 2019 cosmology recognition could be read as already-covered ground.
Fair crediting of a large collaboration versus the three named individuals; I am relying on my own recollection of who led what.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations give a geometric standard ruler that measures the expansion history and constrains dark energy independently of supernovae. The 2005 detections in SDSS and 2dFGRS, combined with the theoretical framework, are a clean observational discovery with lasting impact (DESI now probes possible dynamical dark energy).
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS detection) and Cole/Percival (2dFGRS) are the decisive observational names. The theoretical prediction traces to Sunyaev and Zeldovich and to Peebles and Yu (1970); Peebles is already a laureate and Sunyaev's credit is a real allocation problem, so I propose only the observational trio.
assessment.maturity: Detection is well confirmed by multiple surveys and the method is now standard. The current frontier (hints of evolving dark energy) is unresolved but does not undermine the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should honour the prediction (Sunyaev, Peebles-Yu) or the detection; the supplied credit supports only a partial reading.
Survey-collaboration credit is diffuse; my recollection of 2dFGRS versus SDSS priority is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of matter with protected surface or edge states, predicted theoretically and then observed in HgTe quantum wells and in Bi-based materials. Original, clear and very influential across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction; Molenkamp led the HgTe experimental demonstration of the quantum spin Hall state. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) and Hasan and Moore/Balents/Fu (3D) are legitimate competing claimants, but the supplied names are a coherent theory-plus-experiment trio.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over fifteen-plus years; the interpretation is stable. Applications remain modest, but the conceptual impact is secure and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the HgTe prediction and the three-dimensional topological insulator (names outside the supplied credit).
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize may be argued as already recognising the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat band prediction followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field. Striking theory-experiment pairing, and nature supplied the clue rather than the other way round.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the 2018 experiments. The trio is clean. Cory Dean and others contributed to related moire platforms, and Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's group is the main experimental claim.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving and well replicated, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. It is somewhat early compared with settled discoveries.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Whether a few more years of maturation would produce a clearer picture of credit and meaning.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring the last neutrino mixing angle theta-13 at reactors was a decisive, unambiguous particle-physics discovery that completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the way to CP-violation searches. Clear, quantitative and confirmed.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) are the leading reactor experiments; Double Chooz and T2K (accelerator appearance) are competing claims, which makes a three-person allocation delicate. The supplied trio is defensible as the reactor discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature and stable: precision values have been refined over a decade and agree among reactor and accelerator experiments.
uncertainties: The neutrino oscillation prize in 2015 may be seen as already covering this field.
Priority between Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz is contested in the community.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by discovering a high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, then associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and mapping the Galactic plane. A genuine new window on the universe, with an existential dimension of seeing the cosmos in a new messenger.
assessment.attribution: Only one credited name is supplied; Halzen conceived and led IceCube, but a prize would likely also want to recognise the broader experimental leadership (not in the supplied credit), so the single-laureate configuration is a simplification.
assessment.maturity: Evidence has strengthened over a decade (the 2013 discovery, 2018 source association, 2023 Galactic plane). Individual source identification remains limited, so full maturity is still developing.
uncertainties: Fairness of crediting one person for a large collaboration and a long-developed detector concept.
Source population of the diffuse flux is still not fully identified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonovae explain the radioactive glow of neutron-star mergers and establish them as a main site of r-process heavy-element production, as confirmed by GW170817/AT2017gfo. This links nuclear physics, gravity and the origin of gold with a vivid existential message.
assessment.attribution: Metzger (2010 prediction), Kasen (detailed radiative modelling) and Tanvir (2013 GRB 130603B kilonova candidate) form a plausible set, though Li and Paczynski (1998) as original predictors and many observers of AT2017gfo are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Anchored on a single spectacular event, GW170817, with weaker independent confirmation; the 2017 prize already honoured the gravitational-wave side. Moderately mature.
uncertainties: One well-observed event leaves open the broader r-process budget and spectral interpretation.
Credit for the original prediction versus the discovery is disputed in the wider literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal and its experimental realisation by trapped-ion groups demonstrated that controlled quantum computation and entangling gates are possible in the lab. A foundational tool for quantum information with a clear proposal-to-experiment path.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the decisive theorists; Blatt led the key ion-trap realisations. Wineland (already laureate 2012) and Monroe/Wineland-group contributions complicate fairness, as does overlap with the optical-lattice candidate listing the same theorists.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally mature for two decades, though scalable quantum computing is not yet realised. The 2012 Wineland prize and the 2022 quantum-information prize reduce the freshness of the story.
uncertainties: Overlap with B009, B023 and B041 (same theory names in different packages) and with previous quantum-optics prizes.
Whether ion-trap computation is a discovery or an engineering route to a device.
